title: Exact Characterization of the Holevo Bound by a Quantum Fisher Information Family
abstract: The quantum Cramér-Rao bound constrains the precision of parameter estimation through the symmetric logarithmic derivative quantum Fisher information (SLD QFI). It is asymptotically achievable for regular single-parameter estimation models, but generally not in the multiparameter setting, where optimal measurements for different parameters may be incompatible. For multiparameter estimation, allowing collective measurements, the corresponding asymptotically achievable precision limit is the Holevo bound, whose standard formulation is an optimization over auxiliary Hermitian operators. We bridge this apparent difference in formulation by giving an exact characterization of the Holevo bound in terms of a family of QFIs interpolating between the SLD and right logarithmic derivative (RLD) QFIs. Specifically, for any locally identifiable finite-dimensional estimation problem, we prove that the operator-feasible region in the standard variational definition of the Holevo bound coincides with the intersection of the regions defined by the corresponding Cramér-Rao-type matrix constraints for the entire QFI family. This characterization also applies to rank-deficient states and does not require any prior choice of weight matrix. Consequently, the conventional weight-dependent Holevo bound is recovered by minimizing the corresponding weighted cost over the resulting common feasible region.
summary: This paper rigorously characterizes the Holevo bound for multiparameter quantum parameter estimation by introducing a continuous family of Quantum Fisher Information matrices ($ eta$-LD QFI). It proves that the true bound is determined by the intersection of constraints derived from this entire family, providing a unified geometric understanding of quantum estimation limits.
main_problem: The paper aims to provide an exact characterization of the Holevo bound, which sets the ultimate precision limit for multiparameter quantum parameter estimation.
main_result: The Holevo bound is shown to be equivalent to minimizing a weighted cost over a common feasible region defined by the intersection of constraints derived from an entire family of Quantum Fisher Information matrices ($ eta$-LD QFI).
method: The authors introduce a $ eta$-Logarithmic Derivative ( $ eta$-LD) QFI family that interpolates between known bounds (SLD and RLD QFIs). They reformulate the variational definition of the Holevo bound into a matrix feasibility problem solvable by analyzing this continuous family of constraints.

It then introduces the $ eta$-LD QFI family to bridge this gap, culminating in the main theorem that equates the Holevo bound to the intersection of all $ eta$-LD constraints.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, unified mathematical framework for understanding quantum estimation limits, showing how a continuous family of Fisher information metrics can characterize complex bounds that are otherwise defined via difficult optimization procedures.
